title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 108
paragraphs: When the child was handed over to him, dressed for death, Harpagos went home weeping and told his wife everything Astyages had said. She asked: "What do you intend to do?" He answered: "Not what Astyages commanded. Even if he grows more deranged than he already is, I will not do his bidding or serve him in such a murder. I will not kill this child, for many reasons: the child is my own kin, and Astyages is old and has no male heir. If the throne passes to Mandane after his death—the very woman whose son he now orders me to kill—what is left for me but the greatest danger? For my own safety, the child must die. But one of Astyages' own servants must do the killing, not one of mine."
